claim: GETINT is the routine that collects the player's initials for the high-score table. (The .SBTTL misspells SCORE as CORE; the body comment at :1002 spells it correctly.)

source.verbatim: .SBTTL	GETINT-GET PLAYERS INITIALS FOR HIGH CORE

claim: GETINT displays the message "GREAT SCORE" before collecting initials.
GETINT displays the message "ENTER YOUR INITIALS".
The initials picker commits a letter on a FIRE debounce of 2 frames off then 3 frames on — the trackball/fire input model the keyboard clone replaces.
Initials entry is complete after THREE letters: UPDINT is compared against 3 (RADIX 16, so 03 is 3 in either radix).
Below three letters the routine branches back to keep collecting — the entry does not finish early.
Each newly opened initial slot starts on the letter A.

The initials entry arms a timeout by SEEDING the high byte of the frame counter with 0xF4 (RADIX 16). It is not a count of 244 frames: FRAME+1 advances once per 256 frames (see HS-17) and the entry waits for it to reach zero, so the wait is (0x100-0xF4)*256 = 3072 frames (~51 s at 15750/263 Hz) — matching the line's own "ABOUT 50 SECONDS". Reloaded on each accepted letter.
The letter is scrolled by reading the HORIZONTAL TRACKBALL — the silicon input mechanism the keyboard clone ports away from.
On completion the high scores are copied to the EAROM buffer — the cabinet's persist step, whose clone equivalent is the @arcade/shared/highscore save.

source.verbatim: 62$:	JSR COPYHS		;COPY HIGH SCORES TO EAROM BUFFER

claim: UPDATE is the routine that updates the high-score table when a game ends.
UPDATE takes the qualifying verdict by comparing the finished score against each board entry; a borrow means the new score beats that entry.
The board is walked three bytes per entry across NSCORE entries.
On a qualifying score UPDATE clears UPDINT so GETINT starts with the first initial.
The ROM's high-score table is EIGHT entries deep — shallower than @arcade/shared/highscore's MAX_HIGH_SCORES of 10 (logged as a Delivery Finding).

The entry's INITIAL timeout is seeded by UPDATE with 0xF0, giving (0x100-0xF0)*256 = 4096 frames (~68 s at 15750/263 Hz) — independently corroborating the 256-frame tick model, since the line's own comment calls it one minute at 60Hz.

FRAME is a 16-bit counter incremented once per frame, and FRAME+1 is its HIGH byte — incremented only when the low byte overflows. This is why a timeout seeded into FRAME+1 lasts (0x100-seed)*256 frames rather than `seed` frames.
UPDATE writes the finished score into the high-score table BEFORE any initial is collected, so a timed-out or abandoned initials entry costs the player their NAME but never their PLACE on the board.
The ROM seeds only the FIRST initial slot to 'A' and CLEARS the second and third, so an untouched entry displays "A" plus two blanks — not three A's.

source.verbatim: LDA I,0			;CLEARS SECOND AND THIRD INITIALS
